newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on good sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on good sentiment.

text.p: Shnaghai copper futures ended sharply up on Wednesday on improved market sentiment on expectations of increased copper demand in 1997, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 20,800 yuan ($2,506) per tonne, rising 360 yuan. It opened at 20,520 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 20,500 and a high of 20,820.
Janaury rose 150 to 20,350, February 250 to 20,550, March 390 to 20,780, May 360 to 20,800 and June 330 to 20,790.
Combined volume rose to 82,650 tonnes from 62,650.
Copper opened higher and rose further before all contracts closed at or near their intra-day highs.
Traders said the confidence of long-position holders improved greatly due to expectations of increased domestic copper demand as from early next year.
"Many investors expect demand for copper to increase starting in early 1997, which attracted heavy buying at low levels and short-covering," one trader said.

"Copper has risen sharply since it found strong support at the 19,000-yuan level a week ago," he added. "It breached the key resistance of 20,500 yuan at the opening today, giving great encouragement to long position holders."
Traders said recent LME rises also helped improve sentiment in Shanghai and copper was likely to continue to rise in the next few days.
"Investors have digested the news of rising LME stockpiles and few are expected to want to build short positions," a second trader said.
Aluminium futures ended up. January rose 100 to 13,950 and February 50 to 14,200.
Combined volume rose to 430 tonnes from 20.
